description: Caterpillars feed exclusively on birthwort; in Burgenland the butterfly is tied to warm vineyard margins and field edges in the Pannonian lowlands (Seewinkel/Leithagebirge), very local.

plant: Lotus dorycnium (syn. Dorycnium pentaphyllum) – Prostrate trefoil
description: A key larval host for the variable burnet on warm steppe grasslands and rail embankments in Burgenland; keep sites open and short‑sward.
Larvae feed on thyme; in Burgenland on open steppe grasslands and rocky banks, threatened by scrub encroachment—excellent for sunny gardens and green roofs.

dependent_species: Chrysura cuprea – Ruby‑tailed wasp (parasite of Anthidium)
description: Supports wool‑carder bees (Anthidium) which gather hairs from Stachys leaves; in Burgenland on steppe slopes and dry field margins, very local.

dependent_species: Andrena hattorfiana – Large scabious mining bee
description: Oligolectic bee taking pollen from Knautia/Scabiosa; scattered on extensively managed meadows and orchard belts in Burgenland, threatened by early mowing and fertilization.

description: Alternate core pollen plant; in Burgenland very local on nutrient‑poor calcareous grasslands and dry embankments (Leithagebirge foothills).

Late pollen source supporting A. marginata; scattered along ditches, riverbanks and rail land; popular for wildlife planting in dry soils.

dependent_species: Melitta nigricans – Purple loosestrife silk bee
description: Oligolectic bee on Lythrum; in Burgenland along slow waters, reed margins and ditches (Seewinkel), local; thrives in consistently moist spots.

dependent_species: Macropis europaea – Yellow loosestrife oil bee
description: Oil‑collecting bee strictly bound to Lysimachia; in Burgenland along canals, wet meadows and fen edges, threatened by overgrowth and drainage; good for pond margins.

dependent_species: Osmia adunca – Viper’s bugloss mason bee
description: Specialist pollen bee (oligolectic on Echium); widespread on gravelly/sandy lots, quarries and road verges in Burgenland, but patchy; great for hot balconies in large pots.
Key nectar/pollen in species‑rich margins; scattered on sunny vineyard edges and dry banks; easy culinary herb that benefits long‑tongued bumblebees.
Native to Pannonian regions; deep corollas favored by long‑tongued bees. In Burgenland along warm, dry edges and steppe slopes; excellent garden perennial.
Oligolectic bee collects Campanula pollen; on warm steppe slopes and dry field edges; tall, architectural bellflower for sunny borders.
Supports specialist bees and some moth larvae; in Burgenland local on dry embankments and calcareous grasslands; long‑lived and ornamental.
Larvae on large docks in wetlands; in Burgenland along marsh edges, ditches and wet meadows of the Seewinkel; populations decline with drainage—keep high water tables.
